guides.title: How to fill a Pokémon binder page around one card
guides.lede: Seed one pocket and let michi-maker finish the page around it.
guides.tip: Turn on From my collection and every method draws only from cards you own. VIP adds Pages around this card: every method at once, and you keep the ones you like.

steps.title: Place the seed
steps.body: Fill one pocket with the card the page is about. The middle of a 3×3 reads best.

steps.title: Open Fill page
steps.body: Tap the card, then ✨ Fill page. You only see the methods that suit this card.

steps.title: Pick the idea
steps.body: Same Pokémon, Evolution line, Same artist, Friends and partners, More like this; or Colour by type, Colour match, Full-page spread.

steps.title: Commit it, then keep it or take it back
steps.body: A fill only writes into empty pockets, so nothing you placed moves. It is one step, so one Undo reverses the whole fill and you can try another method.

guides.title: How to cut artwork into binder pockets (Slice Studio)
guides.lede: One picture becomes pocket-sized pieces you arrange like cards.
guides.tip: Slices follow print physics: single pockets or folded sideways pairs, never vertical spans.

steps.title: Open the studio
steps.body: In the Artwork dock on the left, press Slice new art. Or tap any pocket and choose Artwork.

steps.title: Bring in a picture
steps.body: Card art from the catalog, an upload, a pasted URL, or an image dragged in from another tab.

steps.title: Frame it
steps.body: Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, rotate a quarter turn, or press Just the art. The original is only windowed, never changed.

steps.title: Fold a pair if you like
steps.body: Two sideways pockets that open on the same inside edge can take one folded piece.

steps.title: Save slices
steps.body: Every piece lands in the tray of the Artwork dock. Drag one onto any pocket where it fits; it stays in the tray for the next page too.

guides.title: How to print a Pokémon binder fill sheet at true card size
guides.lede: Cut-ready sheets, real card size, so the binder fills in as the cards arrive.
guides.tip: Full-binder PDF export is a paid unlock; the free preview prints a premade example sheet.

steps.title: Open the print sheet
steps.body: Press Print in the binder’s header, or on its tile on My binders. Every page is laid out as fill sheets.

steps.title: Print at 100 percent
steps.body: Actual size, never Fit to page, borderless off. Measure one placeholder: 2.5 by 3.5 inches exactly.

steps.title: Two files, two papers
steps.body: Placeholders are temporary, so plain paper. Art stays for good, so matte cardstock: it sits flat and does not fight a glossy sleeve.

steps.title: Cut and slide
steps.body: Cut along the dashed outlines. Each piece carries its page, row and column; a folded art pair is one piece for two pockets.

steps.title: Swap as cards arrive
steps.body: A placeholder tells you exactly which pocket the real card goes in. The composition never moves.

guides.title: How to search Pokémon cards by set, artist, price and more
guides.lede: Words, fields, comparisons and sorts, stacked until it is exactly what you want.
guides.tip: The cheatsheet puts a Try it button on every example.

steps.title: Just type words
steps.body: charizard, or arita fire. Every word must match somewhere, so more words narrow it.

steps.title: Aim at a field, compare, sort
steps.body: A colon aims a word at one field. Operators compare numbers and dates. sort: orders the result.

steps.title: Filter by your collection
steps.body: have:yes is what you own; have:no with a set is a want-list.

steps.title: Stack and refine
steps.body: Everything combines. Start broad, keep adding until it is exactly the pile you meant.

michiFaq.a: A michi binder is a Pokémon card binder where every page is composed as one picture instead of sorted by set or number: cards, printed artwork, deliberate empty pockets and images sliced across several pockets, arranged so the page looks intentional. The name comes from the collector Michi (@peeplop), who popularised the style.

The michi method is the set of page ideas behind those binders: an anchor page built around one card, a single-Pokémon page, an evolution line, a colour-matched spread, an artist gallery, and a full-page artwork cut into pocket-sized pieces. Michi-Maker builds each of these from one seed card with its Fill page tool.

michiFaq.q: How do I make a michi binder?
michiFaq.a: Pick a page shape (3×3 is the classic, 3×4 for larger binders), place one card you love, and build the rest of the page around it: the same Pokémon, its evolution line, its artist, or cards that share its colours. Print the page at true card size as a fill sheet, slide the paper pieces into the pockets, and swap in the real cards as they arrive.

Yes. Building and sharing binders, the auto-fill methods, and the print preview are free. Paid PRO and VIP plans add full-binder PDF export, binder covers, advanced and artwork-theme search, and more.

michiFaq.q: What size are the printed pieces?
michiFaq.a: Exactly card size: 2.5 by 3.5 inches (63 by 88 mm), printed at 100 percent with no scaling, so each piece fits a standard sleeve or pocket and marks the spot the real card will take.

michiLayouts.name: Anchor page
michiLayouts.body: One card the page is about, everything else chosen to frame it.

michiLayouts.name: Single Pokémon
michiLayouts.body: Every card of one Pokémon: its art across years and artists.

michiLayouts.name: Evolution line
michiLayouts.body: A family read in order, baby to final stage, sometimes with the trainer who owns them.

michiLayouts.name: Colour spread
michiLayouts.body: Cards picked for a shared palette so the whole page reads as one hue.

michiLayouts.name: Artist gallery
michiLayouts.body: One illustrator, the page as their exhibition.

michiLayouts.name: Sliced artwork
michiLayouts.body: A single picture cut into pocket-sized pieces that reassemble across the page.
